correctness.rationale: Let q be the exponent of the finite central commutator subgroup. Class-two commutator calculus makes all powered generators T_i^q commute. On each residue class modulo q, the reduced polynomial is again integer-valued and polynomial independence is preserved. Total ergodicity passes to the powered transformations, so the published commuting theorem gives the same product limit on every residue class; finite recombination gives the full limit.

value.rationale: Finite commutator is a natural structural boundary of an explicit open 2-step nilpotent problem. The theorem resolves all independent polynomial shapes on that boundary and isolates infinite commutator directions as the remaining genuinely noncommutative regime.
residual_risks: The elementary powering argument may exist as unindexed folklore about virtually abelian actions.

final_claim: For a totally ergodic class-two nilpotent action with finite commutator subgroup, every independent integer-polynomial multiple average converges in L2 to the product of integrals.
limitations: Infinite commutator subgroups are not covered.
No non-totally-ergodic seminorm estimate is claimed.
